{{Short description|American statistician (born 1954)}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=September 2022}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=September 2022}}
'''Ruth Mary Mickey''' (born 1954){{r|born}} is a retired American statistician known for her research on [[feature selection]] to control the effects of [[confounding]] on [[statistical inference]],{{r|confounding}} and on the applications of statistics to issues of [[public health]] and [[natural resources]].{{r|abio}} She is a professor emerita in the [[University of Vermont]] Department of Mathematics & Statistics.{{r|profile}}

==Education==
Mickey earned a master's degree in public health at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA) in 1978, and completed a Ph.D. in biostatistics at UCLA in 1983.{{r|ucla}}

==Books==
Mickey is the coauthor of textbooks in statistics including:
*''Applied Statistics: Analysis of Variance and Regression'' (with [[Olive Jean Dunn]] and [[Virginia A. Clark]], Wiley, 3rd ed., 2004){{r|as}}
*''Bayesian Statistics for Beginners: A Step-by-Step Approach'' (with Therese M. Donovan, Oxford University Press, 2019){{r|bsb}}
